html:
"Slavs" is the map's label, for 600 and 700, for the Slavic settlers of the eastern Alps and the upper Sava valley, in today's Slovenia and southern Austria.

They moved in during the late 500s, in the wake of the Avars, who had settled in the plain of Pannonia and ruled many Slav groups. Around 630 a Frankish merchant named Samo led a Slavic revolt against the Avars and ruled a union of tribes for some thirty years. In the Alps a Slavic principality called Carantania grew up, with its own dukes installed in a ceremony on a stone throne.

In the 740s Carantania asked Bavaria for help against the Avars and came under Bavarian and then Frankish rule. Missionaries from Salzburg made it Christian. These Alpine Slavs are the ancestors of today's Slovenes. For the wider story see Early Slavs.
sum: "Slavs" is the map's label, for 600 and 700, for the Slavic settlers of the eastern Alps and the upper Sava valley, in today's Slovenia and southern Austria.
